article.name: CtxVault
article.summary: CtxVault separates local agent memory into semantic document, procedural skill, and bitemporal episodic vaults. It provides CLI, Python, HTTP, and MCP access with vault-level public/restricted access control and local inspection surfaces.

who_what.text: The official README describes CtxVault as local-first memory infrastructure with semantic, skill, and episodic vaults and Python, CLI, HTTP, and MCP interfaces. It states that the agent decides what to write rather than automatic fact extraction.

architecture.text: Vaults are directory-backed independent units: semantic vaults pair source documents with Chroma, skill vaults contain Markdown procedures, and episodic vaults store episodes in SQLite. A registry describes their type, path, and access configuration.

Semantic chunks retain source document identity and caller metadata; skill files use name/description frontmatter; episodes retain content, source, confidence, salience, entity links, metadata, valid and recorded time axes, and optional embeddings. Separate SQLite tables preserve attestations, disputes, and closure/reopen events.

GitHub identifies main as the default branch; the official main Atom feed and full-SHA commit page identify bee8578d49ea35c440d9bee6cd91d4cb139d8744 as current head. Reviewed 2026-11-25T10:23:12Z (UTC; 02:23:12 PST, America/Los_Angeles).

behavior.text: Semantic document indexing extracts text into chunks and writes vector records. API document writes are indexed immediately; documents changed or deleted outside the vault path can leave stale index entries until status/sync or reindex, while vault deletion removes indexed records and the file.
Skill records are named Markdown procedures selected by listing and reading, not by embedding. The reviewed docs do not describe a separate version or archive history for edited skills.

Episodic writes add statements with optional source, entity, confidence, salience, time and metadata. Invalidate closes a statement; supersede closes and links a successor; revise retains validity while changing the recorded version; reopen retains close history; confirmations add dated attestations; unresolved disputes keep both statements open.

Semantic retrieval returns nearest vector chunks with document source and metadata; the vault API defaults to five results. Skill retrieval is list/read. Episodic retrieval applies structured SQLite filters first and ranks the candidate set by relevance, recency, salience, or a weighted composite. Relevance uses cosine similarity when configured vectors exist and word overlap otherwise.

Restricted vaults allow only attached agent names through checked agent-facing read/write interfaces; public vaults are open. CLI and viewer are owner surfaces, HTTP indexing and listing are exceptions, and the HTTP name header is not authentication. A vault, rather than individual rows, is the isolation boundary.

Records preserve source paths, caller metadata, episode sources and event histories. The reviewed material does not establish a shared claim-level citation contract for generated answers; provenance fields alone do not measure answer support.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention — unmeasured. Semantic and episodic retrieval paths are implemented; no answerability or negative-query probes were scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. Episode corrections are modeled through linked lifecycle operations; no correction workload was run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. Semantic deletion removes indexed records; no post-delete probes or physical-storage checks were made.
Scope-isolation leakage — unmeasured. Restricted vault checks are documented; no permitted/forbidden access workload was run.
Evidence support and citation coverage — unmeasured. Source and history metadata exist; no generated answers or citations were scored.
Retrieval latency — unmeasured. No timing samples were collected.
Write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. No timed write/retrieval probes were run.
Tokens and cost — unmeasured. No runtime token usage or charges were collected.
Storage efficiency — unmeasured. No corpus-attributed logical or physical storage size was collected.

limits: Automatic conversation fact extraction and graph-structured semantic memory are not part of the reviewed product description; semantic files can drift from their index if changed outside synchronization.
Access control is vault-level. Agent names are declarations, owner surfaces bypass agent restrictions, and HTTP exceptions require deployment-aware handling.

Episode timestamps are stored and compared as ISO-8601 strings, which require consistent offsets for lexical ordering. The SQLite code recommends UTC; legacy schema-v3 closures may not retain a prior valid_to for reopening.

This bounded review inspected the README, memory-type and access-control documentation, episodic storage/ranking, and semantic vault implementation. It did not trace every endpoint, migration, Chroma query, or deployment configuration.
No runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run; behavior under a deployment, retrieval quality, physical erasure, latency, cost, and storage efficiency remain unverified.
